Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Among patients with RLS, those with insufficient serum vitamin D had significantly higher depression scores (HAMD24) than those with normal vitamin D levels.
Sentence: "The IRLSSG scale score and HAMD24 score were significantly higher in patients with RLS with insufficient serum VitD levels than those with normal serum VitD levels (both P < 0.05)."
Measured as: HAMD24 score
Population: Patients with primary restless legs syndrome
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Normal serum vitamin D level
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Depressive symptoms (CES-D) did not differ between the nutritional supplement group and the placebo group.
Sentence: "For the whole sample, there was a significant improvement in both MCS, mean (95% CI) 2.68 (0.5, 4.9) (p 0.02), and CES-D -2.7 (- 4.5, - 0.9) (p 0.003) during the intervention, but no difference was detected between those who received the nutritional supplement and those who received the placebo."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (CES-D)
Population: Community-dwelling mobility-limited older adults, mean age 77.5, with low serum vitamin D (25(OH)D 22.5-60 nmol/l)
Intervention: Nutritional supplement (protein with vitamin D) for 6 months plus physical activity program
Comparator: Placebo plus physical activity program
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

  "rationale": "Study A is a cross-sectional observational study finding an association with serum vitamin D levels, whereas Study B is a randomized controlled trial testing supplementation and finding no effect.",
